title: What a goal is: four answers, three horizons, five steps
objectives: Turn a wish into a goal with four answers: what, how much, when, how important.
Name the three horizon bands and the main risk of each.
body_md:
A wish (“I want to retire comfortably”) becomes a goal when it has four things: what exactly the money is for (a daughter's engineering degree), how much it costs in today's rupees (₹20 lakh), when it is needed (15 years), and how important it is (must, should or nice-to-have).

| Element | Question | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What | What exactly is the money for? | Daughter's engineering degree |
| How much | What does it cost in today's rupees? | ₹20 lakh |
| When | In how many years is the money needed? | 15 years |
| How important | Is it a must, a should or a nice-to-have? | Must-have |

Goal types by horizon: short (under 3 years — emergency fund, vacation, car, wedding expenses soon; main risk: losing capital just before the money is needed), medium (3–7 years — house down payment, higher studies abroad, starting a business; main risk: a market fall close to the goal date), long (7+ years — children's education, retirement, financial freedom; main risk: inflation, and not taking enough growth). The five-step goal process: Discover (list every goal with the client and their family), Quantify (inflation-adjusted target and date), Prioritise (must-haves first; foundation before everything), Plan (asset mix, then funds, then monthly SIP), Review (every year, and adjust).

| Horizon | Typical goals | Main risk to manage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Short (under 3 years) | Emergency fund, vacation, car, wedding expenses soon | Losing capital just before the money is needed |
| Medium (3–7 years) | House down payment, higher studies abroad, starting a business | A market fall close to the goal date |
| Long (7+ years) | Children's education, retirement, financial freedom | Inflation, and not taking enough growth |

> **Talk-track:** “Before we talk about funds, let's talk about what this money is for and when you'll need it. That decides everything else.”

> **Investor takeaway:** A goal needs an amount, a date and a priority. Without them, no fund can be judged right or wrong.
example: Daughter's engineering degree: ₹20 lakh today, 15 years away, must-have — that is a goal; “retire comfortably” is not yet one.
say: Start with the goal, not the fund.
A goal needs an amount, a date and a priority.
never: A fund name is a goal.
A wish is already a goal.
